title: Cooinaghtyn
description: Ten short stories about memories on the Isle of Man: a woollen mill by a bog, a trip to the pyramids, a wedding fifty years ago, a Greek teacher, a school science club, a grandmother on the town council, a chapel's anniversary, a football match on a ninth birthday, letters from the war and an old lane under the birches.

lessons.title: Yn mwyllin ollan
lessons.summary: Wilfred, eighty, tells his granddaughter Zara about his youth at a woollen mill beside a bog in the north: wet feet on the way to work, sheep giving birth at night, wood carried for the steam and fresh milk at midday; then the two of them walk past the bog to the stones of the old mill.
lessons.text:
Ta Wilfred Hudgeon kiare feed blein d'eash, as t'eh cummal ayns Rhumsaa. Dagh Doonee, ta inneen e vac, Zara, çheet dy akin eh. Ta Zara shey bleeaney jeig d'eash.

Er y Doonee shoh, va'n fliaghey tuittym, as va Zara fliugh tra haink ee stiagh 'sy thie.

“Shenn-ayr,” dooyrt ee, “cre v'ou jannoo 'syn aegid ayd?”

“Ayns my aegid, va mee gobbraghey ec y mwyllin ollan,” dooyrt Wilfred. “Va'n mwyllin ayns glion beg 'sy twoaie, faggys da curragh mooar.”

Tra va Wilfred kiare bleeaney jeig d'eash, hie eh dy obbraghey ec y mwyllin. Dagh laa, v'eh cliaghtey shooyl shaghey yn curragh. Va'n curragh bog as fliugh, as va'n raad fliugh neesht. “Va my chassyn kinjagh fliugh,” dooyrt Wilfred.

Va ram kirree er ny magheryn mygeayrt y mwyllin. Va ny kirree breh eayin 'syn oie, as va Wilfred gobbraghey lesh yn eirinagh tra va kirree breh eayin. 'Sy tourey, va ny eirinee giarrey yn ollan jeh ny kirree, as v'ad cur yn ollan dys y mwyllin.

V'eh cliaghtey ymmyrkey fuygh dys yn aile mooar. Va'n fuygh trome. Va'n aile jannoo ushtey çheh ayns saagh mooar yiarn, as va'n ushtey çheet dy ve gaal. Va'n gaal cur bree da ny greieyn, as va ny greieyn jannoo eaddagh jeh'n ollan.

“Va gaal bane çheet magh ass mullagh y mwyllin,” dooyrt Wilfred. “Va sleih fakin y gaal veih'n raad.”

Ec mean y laa, va ben yn eirinagh cur bainney da ny guillyn. “Cha row bainney erbee rieau cho mie as y bainney shen,” dooyrt Wilfred.

Ghow Wilfred brat shenn, jeant jeh ollan. “Shoh ollan veih'n mwyllin,” dooyrt eh. Hug Zara e laue er y brat. “T'eh çheh as bog,” dooyrt ee.

“Vel y mwyllin ayn foast?” dooyrt Zara.

“Cha nel,” dooyrt Wilfred. “Cha nel agh claghyn ayn nish. Agh ta'n curragh ayn foast, as ta'n raad goll shaghey eh.”

Er y Doonee ny lurg shen, hie Zara as Wilfred dys y glion. Hie ad shaghey yn curragh, as va'n raad fliugh reesht. Va Zara fakin ny claghyn shenn jeh'n mwyllin. “Ayns my aegid, va'n boayl shoh lane dy obbyr,” dooyrt Wilfred.

Feyshtyn:
Row'n mwyllin faggys da curragh?
Va. Va'n mwyllin ayns glion beg faggys da curragh mooar.
Cre va Wilfred cliaghtey ymmyrkey dys yn aile?
V'eh cliaghtey ymmyrkey fuygh dys yn aile mooar.
Cre va cur bree da ny greieyn?
Va'n gaal cur bree da ny greieyn.
Cre va ben yn eirinagh cur da ny guillyn?
Va ee cur bainney daue.
Vel y mwyllin ayn foast?
Cha nel. Cha nel agh claghyn ayn nish.

lessons.title: Ny pyramidyn
lessons.summary: Hilda shows her grandson Theo an old photograph from a trip to Egypt: the great heat, a first glimpse of the pyramids from a bus in the desert, a faint in the sand, and the strange palace of a rich prince.
lessons.text:
Ta Hilda Boyde 75 bleeaney d'eash, as t'ee cummal ayns Doolish. Er y voalley 'sy thie eck, ta jalloo shenn. Ayns y jalloo, ta Hilda as e fer-poosee, Percy, ec ny pyramidyn ayns Egypt.

Haink Theo, mac e inneen, dy akin ee. “Cre'n jalloo shoh?” dooyrt eh.

“Shoh mee as y shenn-ayr ayd ayns Egypt, 'sy vlein 1976,” dooyrt Hilda. “She yn traa share va rieau ain.”

Va Hilda as Percy aeg ec y traa shen. Hie ad dys Egypt son jeih laa. Va'n çhiass feer vooar. Cha row Hilda rieau ayns çhiass myr shen. Ec mean y laa, va'n çhiass ro vooar, as va ny sleih ooilley cummal 'sy thie.

Er y nah laa, hie ad ayns bus magh 'sy faasagh. Cha row agh geinnagh 'sy faasagh, as cha row ushtey erbee. Eisht, trooid uinnag y vus, hooar Hilda skell jeh ny pyramidyn. Va'n skell giare, agh cha row Hilda rieau er vakin red myr shen. Tra hie'n bus ny s'faggys, v'ad fakin ny pyramidyn slane. Va ny pyramidyn mooar as yindyssagh.

“Yindyssagh!” dooyrt Percy.

Dooyrt y fer-stiurey dy row ny pyramidyn troggit son reeaghyn roish thousaneyn dy vleeantyn.

Va'n çhiass 'sy faasagh feer lajer. Lurg tammylt, va Hilda ching, as huitt ee ayns neeal er y geinnagh. Hug Percy ushtey er e eddin, as lurg tammylt beg, ren ee e sooillyn y osley.

“Huitt oo ayns neeal,” dooyrt Percy. “Ta feme ayd er ushtey.”

Er y laa ny lurg shen, hie ad dy akin plaase ayns yn ard-valley. Va'n plaase ec prinse berçhagh roish keead blein. Va'n prinse feer verçhagh: va airh er ny boallaghyn, as va reddyn quaagh ayns dagh shamyr. Va kayt quaagh jeant jeh clagh, as va ushag quaagh lesh kione dooinney.

“Ta'n plaase shoh quaagh,” dooyrt Percy, “agh she prinse berçhagh v'ayn!”

“Vel oo goll dys Egypt reesht?” dooyrt Theo.

“Cha nel,” dooyrt Hilda. “Ta'n çhiass ro vooar dou nish. Agh ta'n jalloo aym foast, as ta ny cooinaghtyn aym foast.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n blein hie Hilda as Percy dys Egypt?
Hie ad dys Egypt 'sy vlein 1976.
Row'n çhiass mooar?
Va. Va'n çhiass feer vooar.
Cre hooar Hilda trooid uinnag y vus?
Hooar ee skell jeh ny pyramidyn.
Cre haghyr da Hilda 'sy faasagh?
Huitt ee ayns neeal er y geinnagh.
Quoi va cummal ayns y plaase?
Va prinse berçhagh cummal ayns y plaase roish keead blein.

lessons.title: Laa yn phoosey
lessons.summary: Fifty years after her wedding, Doreen tells her granddaughter Esther about the busy week before it, the long dress her mother shortened, the ring, her father's welcome, the band, the wine, and a speech about honour.
lessons.text:
Ta Doreen as Raymond Garrow poost rish 50 blein. Er y Jesarn shoh, bee feaill mooar oc ayns Pheeil. Haink Esther, inneen nyn mac, dy obbraghey marish Doreen.

“Shenn-voir,” dooyrt Esther, “cre'n aght va laa yn phoosey ayd?”

“Va'n shiaghtin roish y poosey feer trome,” dooyrt Doreen. “Dagh laa 'sy shiaghtin shen, va obbyr noa ain. Ren my voir y garmad poosee aym. Va'n garmad bane, as v'eh jeant jeh sheeidey. Agh va liurid y garmad ro vooar. V'eh ro liauyr, as va mee tuittym tra va mee shooyl ayn. Ren my voir liurid y garmad y ghiarrey, as eisht va'n garmad kiart.”

Er laa yn phoosey, hie Doreen as e ayr dys y cheeill. Va Raymond ec y cheeill roue. Hug Raymond fainey airh er mair Doreen. “Ta'n fainey aym foast,” dooyrt Doreen, as hug ee e laue roish Esther. Va'n fainey beg as shenn, agh v'eh soilshaghey 'sy ghrian.

Lurg y cheeill, va feaill mooar ayns thie mooar 'sy valley. Va ayr Doreen ec y dorrys. Dooyrt eh “Failt erriu!” rish dy chooilley pheiagh. Va failt vie ec dy chooilley pheiagh 'sy thie.

Va bann beg ayns y thie mooar. Va kiare fir 'sy vann, as v'ad cloie kiaull shenn as kiaull noa. Ren dy chooilley pheiagh daunsey: ny paitçhyn, ny sleih aegey as ny sleih shenn.

Va feeyn jiarg as feeyn bane er ny buird. Va ayr Doreen giu feeyn jiarg. Dagh tammylt, v'eh gra “Tooilley feeyn!” as va ny sleih gearey. “Tooilley kiaull!” v'eh gra rish y vann neesht.

Eisht, ren braar Raymond loayrt rish ny sleih. “She onnor mooar eh dou dy ve ayns shoh jiu,” dooyrt eh. “Ta Raymond er gheddyn ben vie. Ta onnor mooar ec y lught-thie ain.”

“Va'n laa shen yn laa share 'sy vea aym,” dooyrt Doreen.

Er y Jesarn, va'n feaill feer vie. Va bann ayn reesht, as va feeyn er ny buird reesht. Ren Doreen as Raymond daunsey, myr roish 50 blein.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ren y garmad poosee?
Ren moir Doreen y garmad poosee.
Row liurid y garmad kiart?
Cha row. Va'n garmad ro liauyr.
Cre dooyrt ayr Doreen ec y dorrys?
Dooyrt eh “Failt erriu!” rish dy chooilley pheiagh.
Quoi va 'sy vann?
Va kiare fir 'sy vann.
Cre dooyrt braar Raymond?
Dooyrt eh dy nee onnor mooar eh dy ve ayns shen.

lessons.title: Yn ynseyder Greagish
lessons.summary: Cyril, now a translator, remembers Mrs Fletcher, who taught him Greek at school in Douglas: the hard spelling and grammar, the nominative, an old literary story full of characters, and how she kept order, made him pay attention and encouraged him.
lessons.text:
Ta Cyril Walsh 68 bleeaney d'eash. T'eh ny screeudeyr, as t'eh çhyndaa lioaryn veih Greagish gys Baarle as Gaelg. T'eh cooinaghtyn er yn ynseyder Greagish echey 'sy scoill ayns Doolish, Mavis Fletcher.

Tra va Cyril tree bleeaney jeig d'eash, ren eh toshiaght dy ynsaghey Greagish. Va Greagish doillee. Va lettraghey ny focklyn Greagish doillee dasyn, as cha nel ny lettyryn Greagish myr ny lettyryn Baarle. Va grammar Greagish doillee neesht.

“Cre'n resoon ta mee ynsaghey Greagish?” dooyrt Cyril rish yn ynseyder. “Cha nel peiagh erbee loayrt Greagish shenn nish.”

“Ta resoon mie ayd,” dooyrt Mavis Fletcher. “Ta ny skeealyn share 'sy theihll screeuit ayns Greagish shenn. Ec jerrey y vlein, bee oo lhaih ad.”

Va smaght eck er ny paitçhyn. Cha row ny paitçhyn loayrt tra v'ee loayrt. Tra va guilley jeeaghyn magh trooid yn uinnag, v'ee gra, “Cur geill!” As va dy chooilley phaitçhey cur geill. Va smaght eck, agh v'ee mie rish ny paitçhyn.

Dagh shiaghtin, v'ee jannoo prowal er grammar as er lettraghey. Ta cummey ennymagh ec dagh ennym ayns Greagish. “Cre'n cummey ennymagh ta ec y fockle shoh?” v'ee gra. Cha row lettraghey Cyril kiart dy mennick, agh v'ee greinnaghey eh. “T'ou ynsaghey,” v'ee gra. “Ta'n lettraghey ayd ny share dagh shiaghtin.” Va'n greinnaghey shen mie da.

Ec jerrey y vlein, ren ad skeeal lettyragh shenn y lhaih. Va ram karracteyryn 'sy skeeal: ree, ben-ree, sidooryn as jee. Va'n karracteyr share lesh Cyril ny shiaulteyr va shiaull harrish y keayn son jeih bleeaney. Va Greagish lettyragh doillee, agh va'n skeeal yindyssagh.

Nish ta Cyril çhyndaa skeealyn lettyragh veih Greagish. T'eh smooinaghtyn er Mavis Fletcher dagh laa. “Tra ta mee gobbraghey er grammar doillee,” t'eh gra, “ta mee clashtyn ee: ‘Cur geill!’”

Feyshtyn:
Quoi va'n ynseyder Greagish ec Cyril?
Va Mavis Fletcher yn ynseyder Greagish echey.
Row lettraghey ny focklyn Greagish aashagh?
Cha row. Va lettraghey ny focklyn Greagish doillee da Cyril.
Cre va Mavis Fletcher gra tra va guilley jeeaghyn magh trooid yn uinnag?
V'ee gra, “Cur geill!”
Cre'n karracteyr va share lesh Cyril?
Va'n shiaulteyr share lesh Cyril.
Cre ta Cyril jannoo nish?
T'eh çhyndaa skeealyn lettyragh veih Greagish.

lessons.title: Yn club oaylleeaght
lessons.summary: Gladys, who works in technology, remembers the science club of her childhood: Mr Kinnaird showed them magnetic iron and its particles, friction that makes heat, the plasma of the sun, and numerical questions about a finite world, and told them that the hardest processes are only many small steps.
lessons.text:
Ta Gladys Bell gobbraghey ayns çhaghnoaylleeaght. T'ee jannoo greieyn noa son fir-lhee. Tra va Gladys aeg, va club oaylleeaght ec y scoill eck ayns Doolish. Dagh Jeheiney, va'n club ec Leonard Kinnaird, yn ynseyder fishig. T'ee cooinaghtyn er y club dagh laa.

Er y chied laa, hug Leonard Kinnaird peesh yiarn magnaidagh er y voayrd. Hug eh ayrneenyn beggey yiarn er duillag phabyr. Eisht, hug eh y yiarn magnaidagh fo'n phabyr. Ren ny ayrneenyn yiarn scughey! Hie ny ayrneenyn ooilley 'sy troa cheddin, as v'ad jannoo cummey er y phabyr.

“Shen yn troa ta'n yiarn magnaidagh cur da ny ayrneenyn,” dooyrt Leonard. “Ta'n seihll hene magnaidagh neesht.”

Er laa elley, dooyrt eh rish ny paitçhyn dy chur nyn laueyn ry-cheilley as dy scughey ad. “Vel nyn laueyn çheh?” dooyrt eh. “Ta. Shen freayn. Ta freayn jannoo çheh.” Ren eh soilshaghey daue dy vel freayn ayns dy chooilley ghreie.

Er laa elley, loayr eh mychione y ghrian. “Cha nel y ghrian aile,” dooyrt eh. “T'ee jeant jeh plasmey. Ta plasmey feer çheh, as ta ayrneenyn beggey scughey ayn.” Va Gladys smooinaghtyn dy row plasmey yindyssagh.

Va prowallyn earrooagh ec Leonard neesht: “Cre wheesh ushtey t'ayns y keayn? Cre wheesh bee t'ayns y seihll son ooilley ny sleih?” Va ny prowallyn earrooagh doillee. “Ta'n seihll caglit,” dooyrt eh. “Ta'n ushtey as y thalloo caglit. Ta feme ain smooinaghtyn er shen.”

Laa dy row, dooyrt Gladys, “Ta oaylleeaght ro chast dou.”

“Ta ram obbraidyn cast,” dooyrt Leonard. “Agh ta dagh obbraid cast jeant jeh ram reddyn beggey. Jean un red beg, as eisht red beg elley.”

Nish, tra ta obbraid cast ec Gladys 'syn obbyr eck, t'ee smooinaghtyn er ny focklyn echey. T'ee jannoo un red beg, as eisht red beg elley. Ta çhaghnoaylleeaght cast, agh ta Gladys gra dy nee Leonard Kinnaird hug ee er y raad shen.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi va stiurey yn club oaylleeaght?
Va Leonard Kinnaird, yn ynseyder fishig, stiurey yn club.
Cre ren ny ayrneenyn yiarn?
Hie ny ayrneenyn ooilley 'sy troa cheddin.
Cre ta freayn jannoo?
Ta freayn jannoo çheh.
Cre jeh ta'n ghrian jeant?
Ta'n ghrian jeant jeh plasmey.
Cre ta Gladys jannoo nish?
T'ee gobbraghey ayns çhaghnoaylleeaght.

lessons.title: Yn choonceil
lessons.summary: Lillian remembers her grandmother Edith, who sat on Peel's town council for a small nationalist party: she was its spokeswoman, argued for a republic against the conservatives, demanded a school taught through Manx, and wept when the news was announced; the official letter now hangs in that school, where Lillian teaches.
lessons.text:
Ta Lillian Harrison lhaih lettyryn shenn ec y thie eck ayns Pheeil. She lettyryn e shenn-voir, Edith Harrison, ad. Va Edith er coonceil y valley ayns Pheeil rish feed blein.

Ta Lillian cooinaghtyn er Edith. Va Edith ny loayrtagh son partee beg. Va ashoonaghys ec cree y phartee. Va'n partee laccal dy beagh Ellan Vannin ny çheer slane hene. Va Edith pobblaghtagh neesht. “Cha nel feme ain er ree ny ben-ree,” v'ee gra. “Ta mee pobblaghtagh, as ta ashoonaghys aym.”

Va ram sleih cumaadagh er y choonceil. Cha row ny sleih cumaadagh laccal caghlaa erbee. Va Edith kinjagh loayrt noi ny sleih cumaadagh. Agh va Edith gra, “T'ad cumaadagh, agh t'ad sleih mie.”

Va Edith gra dy row cooishyn bunraghtoil ayns ashoonaghys. “Quoi ta reill Ellan Vannin? Shen cooish bunraghtoil,” v'ee gra. Hie ee dys çhionnal mooar ayns Doolish dy loayrt mychione ny cooishyn bunraghtoil shen. Va keead peiagh ec y çhionnal, as va Edith yn loayrtagh son y phartee eck.

Va Edith aggyrt scoill son ny paitçhyn, as ynsagh trooid y Ghaelg ayn. “Ta mee aggyrt scoill Gaelg,” dooyrt ee 'sy choonceil. Cha row ny sleih cumaadagh laccal scoill noa, agh va Edith aggyrt eh dagh blein.

Ta lettyr oikagh ayns laue Lillian. Haink y lettyr oikagh veih'n reiltys 'sy vlein 1995. Ta'n lettyr gra dy bee scoill Gaelg ayn. Va'n naight fogrit 'sy choonceil er y laa shen. Tra va'n naight fogrit, ren Edith keayney.

Va Lillian ayns y scoill shen. Nish t'ee ny ynseyder 'sy scoill. Ta'n lettyr oikagh er y voalley 'sy scoill nish.

Feyshtyn:
Cre cho liauyr as va Edith er y choonceil?
Va Edith er y choonceil rish feed blein.
Cre va Edith 'sy phartee?
V'ee ny loayrtagh son y phartee.
Row ny sleih cumaadagh laccal caghlaa?
Cha row. Cha row ny sleih cumaadagh laccal caghlaa erbee.
Cre va Edith aggyrt?
V'ee aggyrt scoill Gaelg son ny paitçhyn.
Cre ren Edith tra va'n naight fogrit?
Ren ee keayney.

lessons.title: Y cheeill ayns y glion
lessons.summary: At the 150th anniversary of the founding of a chapel in a glen, Stanley, eighty-five, remembers the congregation of his boyhood, his family's line of builders and missionaries, communion, the bishop, and how everyone stood together to sing.
lessons.text:
Ta keeill veg ayns glion 'sy jiass. Er y Doonee shoh, ta feaill ec y cheeill. She feaill son bunneeaght y cheeill, roish 150 blein.

Ta Stanley Lowther 85 bleeaney d'eash. Ta ram cooinaghtyn echey mychione y cheeill. Tra v'eh ny ghuilley, va cohionnal mooar ec y cheeill. Va keead peiagh 'sy chohionnal dagh Doonee. Nish cha nel agh feed peiagh 'sy chohionnal.

Ta Stanley jeh sluight shenn 'sy glion. Ren shenn-ayr e ayr y cheeill y hroggal. Ta'n sluight echey er ve 'sy glion rish 300 blein. Va mishoon ec braar e ayr. Hie eh dys Affrick er mishoon, as v'eh ynsaghey paitçhyn ayns shen. Haink eh thie 'sy vlein 1950, as v'eh loayrt mychione y vishoon echey ayns y cheeill.

Ta Stanley cooinaghtyn er y chied commeeys echey. V'eh daa vlein jeig d'eash. Va'n aspick er jeet veih Doolish. Ghow Stanley yn commeeys veih'n aspick. “Va aggle orrym,” dooyrt Stanley. “Cha row yn aspick rieau ec y cheeill roish.”

Jiu, ta'n aspick noa çheet dys y feaill. Ta sleih veih dagh keeill 'syn aspickys çheet. Ta'n aspickys mooar, agh ta ny sleih unnaneyssit son y laa.

Ec y feaill, ta Stanley loayrt rish y chohionnal. “Ta'n cheeill shoh fondagh,” t'eh gra. “Ta ny boallaghyn fondagh, as ta'n cohionnal fondagh neesht. Tra va mee aeg, va'n cohionnal unnaneyssit. Va shin ooilley unnaneyssit, ayns traa mie as ayns traa olk.”

Eisht, ta'n aspick gra, “Shassee seose, son yn arrane!” Hass dy chooilley pheiagh seose. Hass Stanley seose neesht. Ren ny sleih arrane shenn y ghoaill, as va Stanley goaill eh maroo, myr tra v'eh ny ghuilley.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n feaill t'ec y cheeill?
She feaill son bunneeaght y cheeill.
Row cohionnal mooar ec y cheeill tra va Stanley ny ghuilley?
Va. Va keead peiagh 'sy chohionnal.
Quoi ren y cheeill y hroggal?
Ren shenn-ayr ayr Stanley y cheeill y hroggal.
Cre'n mishoon va ec braar e ayr?
Hie eh dys Affrick er mishoon, as v'eh ynsaghey paitçhyn.
Cre ren ny sleih tra dooyrt yn aspick “Shassee seose”?
Hass dy chooilley pheiagh seose.

lessons.title: Yn staid
lessons.summary: Ralph remembers his ninth birthday, when his father Bertie took him to a big stadium in England: a red cloth round his neck, a temporary captain, a team not likely to win, a late chance, and getting lost in the crowd afterwards.
lessons.text:
Ta Ralph Pryce jeeaghyn er cloie bluckan er y çhellveeish. Ta'n cloie ayns staid mooar ayns Sostyn. Ta Ralph cooinaghtyn er y chied cheayrt v'eh ayns y staid shen.

Va'n laa shen yn nuyoo laa ruggyree echey. Er yn nuyoo laa ruggyree echey, ghow e ayr, Bertie, eh dys y staid er y lhong as er y traen. Hug Bertie eaddagh jiarg mygeayrt mwannal Ralph. “Freill yn eaddagh shoh mygeayrt y mwannal ayd,” dooyrt Bertie. “Bee eh feayr 'sy staid.”

Va'n staid feer vooar. Va thousaneyn dy leih ayns shen. Va'n staid lhieent dy leih. Va ny sleih lhieeney ny raaidyn ooilley mygeayrt y staid.

Va'n toshee oc ching, as va toshee shallidagh oc son y cloie. Va'n toshee shallidagh aeg. “Cha nel eh liklee dy jean ad cosney jiu,” dooyrt Bertie. “Ta'n skimmee elley ny share.”

Va'n cloie doillee. Va'n bluckan goll harrish y cagliagh dagh tammylt. Lurg tammylt liauyr, cha row goal erbee ec skimmee erbee. Eisht, hooar y toshee shallidagh caa. Hooar eh yn bluckan faggys da'n cagliagh, as ren eh roie shaghey dooinney as dooinney elley. Va caa echey, as ghow eh yn caa. Goal!

Va ny sleih ooilley 'sy staid gearey as goaill arraneyn. Ren Bertie as Ralph lheim seose. “Cha row eh liklee!” dooyrt Bertie.

Lurg y cloie, va ram sleih goll magh ass y staid. Va Ralph caillt mastey ny sleih. Cha row e ayr ry-akin. Va Ralph caillt as v'eh keayney. Agh va'n eaddagh jiarg mygeayrt y mwannal echey, as va Bertie fakin yn eaddagh jiarg. “Ralph!” dooyrt eh. Nish cha row Ralph caillt.

“Va'n laa shen feeu eh,” dooyrt Ralph nish. “Va'n raad liauyr, agh va dy chooilley oor feeu.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n laa ruggyree v'ec Ralph?
V'eh yn nuyoo laa ruggyree echey.
Cre hug Bertie er mwannal Ralph?
Hug eh eaddagh jiarg mygeayrt mwannal Ralph.
Row'n staid lhieent?
Va. Va'n staid lhieent dy leih.
Quoi hooar y goal?
Hooar y toshee shallidagh y goal.
Cre haghyr da Ralph lurg y cloie?
Va Ralph caillt mastey ny sleih.

lessons.title: Lettyryn 'sy chaggey
lessons.summary: Violet remembers the war years in Douglas: food reduced by restrictions, letters from her father delivered by the postman, her mother who refused to read the private ones aloud, news of destruction in England, and a letter she found a year after the war in the shadow at the bottom of the box.
lessons.text:
Ta Violet Hardy 90 bleeaney d'eash. Ta kishtey beg eck lane dy lettyryn shenn. Ta ny lettyryn veih'n chaggey, tra va Violet ny inneen veg ayns Doolish.

Ayns y chaggey, va lhiettrimys er bee. Va lhiettrimys er arran, er bainney as er feill. Va'n bee leodit dagh blein. “Hoshiaght, va'n bee leodit beggan,” t'ee gra. “Eisht va'n bee leodit reesht, as va shin kinjagh laccal bee.”

Va ayr Violet ayns yn armee. V'eh screeu lettyr gys y lught-thie dagh shiaghtin. Va'n fer-postagh livrey ny lettyryn. Dagh Jeheiney, va Violet shassoo ec y dorrys, as va'n fer-postagh livrey lettyr. “Va mee kinjagh ec y dorrys,” t'ee gra.

Va moir Violet lhaih ny lettyryn. Va ram jeu preevaadjagh. Va Violet laccal clashtyn ny lettyryn preevaadjagh, agh ren e moir jiooldey. “Ta'n lettyr shoh preevaadjagh,” v'ee gra. Cha row ee jiooldey ny lettyryn elley: v'ee lhaih ad ooilley da Violet.

Va ayr Violet screeu mychione y chaggey. Va cragh mooar ayns ny ard-valjyn ayns Sostyn. Va thieyn as straidyn ayns cragh. “Ta'n cragh feer olk,” v'eh screeu.

Lurg y chaggey, haink ayr Violet thie. Blein ny lurg shen, va Violet glenney y kishtey. V'ee fakin lettyr ayns y scaa ec bun y kishtey. Cha row ee er vakin eh ny s'leaie. Ren ee cronnaghey dy row eh screeuit ny s'leaie na ny lettyryn elley: v'eh screeuit 'sy chied vlein jeh'n chaggey. Ren ee cronnaghey neesht dy row eh preevaadjagh: va'n ennym eck er.

Va'n lettyr gra: “My ta mee geddyn baase, insh da Violet dy vel graih aym urree.” Agh cha dooar ayr Violet baase. Nish ta'n lettyr shen ec Violet ayns y kishtey.

Feyshtyn:
Row lhiettrimys er bee ayns y chaggey?
Va. Va lhiettrimys er arran, er bainney as er feill.
Quoi va livrey ny lettyryn?
Va'n fer-postagh livrey ny lettyryn.
Cre ren moir Violet tra va Violet laccal clashtyn ny lettyryn preevaadjagh?
Ren ee jiooldey.
Row cragh ayns Sostyn?
Va. Va cragh mooar ayns ny ard-valjyn.
Cre'n boayl va'n lettyr?
Va'n lettyr ayns y scaa ec bun y kishtey.

lessons.title: Y bayr shenn
lessons.summary: Arnold walks with his granddaughter Ada down the lane of his childhood under the birches; he shows her the buds, the birds whose habitat the lane is, and tells how the lane's users once saved it, for the sake of the environment, from becoming a road.
lessons.text:
Ta Arnold Kneebone 70 bleeaney d'eash. Er y Jeheiney shoh, t'eh shooyl lesh inneen e inneen, Ada. T'ad shooyl er y bayr shenn faggys da'n thie echey. “Lhig dou y bayr shoh y hoilshaghey dhyt,” dooyrt eh. “Va mee cliaghtey shooyl er y bayr shoh dagh laa tra va mee aeg.”

Ta biljyn beih faggys da'n bayr. Ta ny biljyn beih ard as bane. “Tra va mee aeg, va ny biljyn beih shoh beg,” dooyrt Arnold. “Nish t'ad ard.”

She yn arragh eh. Ta buinnaghyn beggey glassey er ny biljyn. “Jeeagh er ny buinnaghyn,” dooyrt Arnold. “Ayns shiaghtin, bee duillagyn er dagh buinney.”

Ta ushagyn çheet as goll fud ny biljyn. Ta ushagyn ayns ny biljyn as fud ny duillagyn. “She oayll ny ushagyn y bayr shoh,” dooyrt Arnold. “Ta ram cretooryn beggey cummal 'sy bayr. Ta'n oayll oc beg, agh t'ee mie.”

“Row raad mooar rieau er y bayr shoh?” dooyrt Ada.

“Cha row,” dooyrt Arnold. “Agh roish feed blein, va'n reiltys laccal raad mooar noa 'sy boayl shoh. Agh va ram ymmydeyryn ec y bayr: sleih shooyl, sleih er cabbil, paitçhyn cloie. Haink ny ymmydeyryn ooilley ry-cheilley. Dooyrt ad, ‘Lhig dooin y bayr y reayll!’”

Va ny ymmydeyryn loayrt mychione y çhymmyltaght. Dooyrt ad dy row y bayr mie son y çhymmyltaght, as dy row eh oayll son ushagyn as cretooryn. Lurg tammylt, dooyrt y reiltys, “Lhig da'n bayr ve.”

“Lhig dooin shooyl ny sodjey,” dooyrt Ada. Hie ad fud ny biljyn beih, as v'ad clashtyn ny ushagyn. Va'n çhymmyltaght glen as mie.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta faggys da'n bayr?
Ta biljyn beih faggys da'n bayr.
Cre ta er ny biljyn 'syn arragh?
Ta buinnaghyn beggey glassey er ny biljyn.
Cre dooyrt Arnold mychione y bayr?
Dooyrt eh dy nee oayll ny ushagyn eh.
Quoi haink ry-cheilley dy reayll y bayr?
Haink ny ymmydeyryn ooilley ry-cheilley.
